Privacy

What Relay sees, and what it keeps to itself.

Last updated 6 October 2026. Relay is a private beta run by a four-person team; this notice describes what we actually do today, and we will update it before we do anything else.

The short version

Relay sits in a group chat to help a group decide on a trip. What you tell Relay in a one-to-one message is never posted to the group. We use it to work out which options suit everyone, and the group only ever sees the conclusion — not whose constraint produced it.

In a group chat

When an organiser adds Relay to a group, Relay can see messages sent in that group while it is a member. We store:

  • the trip being planned, and who is part of it;
  • messages addressed to Relay, and replies that are votes or answers to its questions;
  • the options Relay proposed, who approved what, and when.

Relay stays quiet in the thread unless it is addressed or it has something to decide. We do not use the contents of your group chat to train general-purpose models.

In a private message

Relay asks each traveller directly for departure city, dates, budget and preferences. That is held against your person record for the trip and is not revealed to other members of the group, including the organiser. Relay may reflect it back as an aggregate — “this week clears all five calendars” — without attributing it.

The waitlist form

If you sign up on this site we store your email address and whatever else you chose to give us: name, group size, which chat app your group uses, when the trip is, and your note. We also record your browser’s user-agent string and which page you submitted from, to tell real signups from bots.

We use it to decide who to onboard first and to email you about Relay. We do not sell it, share it with advertisers, or add you to anyone else’s list. Reply to any email from us, or write to tlong7@uw.edu, and we will delete you.

Who else processes it

  • Supabase — our database and hosting.
  • The messaging provider for the channel your group uses, which carries the messages themselves.
  • A large language model provider, which processes message content to extract constraints, draft options and read votes. Content sent for this purpose is not used to train their models.

How long we keep it

Trip data is kept while the trip is live and for 12 months after, so a returning group starts from what was already decided. Waitlist entries are kept until you ask us to remove them or until we close the beta list. Ask us to delete a trip and we delete it, including the private constraints attached to it.

Your rights

You can ask for a copy of what we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it. One email to tlong7@uw.edu is enough; we aim to answer within seven days. If you are in the UK or EU you also have the right to complain to your local data protection authority.

Children

Relay is not for people under 16. If a group includes someone under 16, do not add Relay to it.

Changes

If we change how any of this works we will update this page and date it. Material changes get an email to everyone on the list.
